structured_stats.description:
The '''Saboteur''' is a poison-based tower bought for {{Coins|7,500}} after triumphing [[Polluted Wasteland II]] or bought for {{Robux|449}}.

It fires in a manner similar to the [[Shotgunner]]. With each shot, multiple bullets come out of its spread gun. These shots are spread out and not guaranteed to all hit the same enemy. Additionally, it has a max hits stats which is used in its ''Scattershot''. With it, the damage dealt by a pellet is done as many times as what the max hits is. For example, at Level 4, the max hits is 3, meaning each pellet deals damage three times to the enemy it hits. The max hits being 3 does not however mean it will only hit three enemies, as each of the 6 pellets can, even if this happens rarely, all hit a different enemy

With each shot, the '''Saboteur''' applies poison, which deals damage over time while also slowing enemies down. Unlike the [[Toxic Gunner]] however, it cannot melt [[Defense]].

Starting from Level 3, it gains the ''Aggressive Toxins'' ability. When used, a cursor will appear allowing the '''Saboteur''' to throw a grenade anywhere in its range. This will apply the [[Neuralyzed]] attribute to the enemy, making towers target them while also increasing how much damage they receive. Enemies with [[Neuralyzed]] take priority over enemies with [[Aggro]]. This ability costs {{Money|500}} to use.

The '''Saboteur''' has a placement limit of 8.

==Description==
The '''Damage Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's damage, making them stronger. It is displayed on the tower itself with the icon of an arm with muscle.

==Mechanics==
'''Damage Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 + Damage Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Buff''' is the debuff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The damage increased by the '''Damage Buff''' will always round down to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Buff''' will deal 7 damage, instead of 7.5.

Multiple towers are not fully affected by the buff. A full list of towers affected fully, partially or that are unaffected can be found below.

==Description==
'''Defense''' is a status value given to certain enemies and units. Enemies may spawn with this naturally, or be granted this through a litany of means.

==Mechanics==
There are two types of defense statistic. The main defense statistic is ''Percentage Defense'' which is used to calculate ''Effective Damage''.

''Percentage Defense'' is the actual defense percentage you see on an enemy or unit. However, this does not mean that if an enemy has 50% defense damage dealt towards it will be decreased 50%. In reality, the number listed is far closer to the percentage of additional health that '''Defense''' gives it.

''Effective Damage'' is the actual damage dealt towards an enemy by a tower once ''Percentage Defense'' is applied. ''Effective Damage'' is calculated by calculating

::<big>'''Original Damage ÷ (1 + Percentage Defense)'''</big>

where ''Percentage Defense'' is changed from a percentage into its equivalent decimal number (for instance, 50% would be 0.5 in decimal form). For example, a tower that deals 100 damage attacking an enemy with 50% defense would deal 67 damage as 100 ÷ (1 + 0.5) = 66.67 to two decimal places. Due to ''Effective Damage'' always being rounded up to the nearest integer, 66.67 rounds up to 67. Prior to the [[v1.1.0|Entity System Update]], ''Effective Damage'' was always rounded down to the nearest integer.

Unit defense works identically to enemy defense, reducing damage from enemy abilities and collision.

A list of certain ''Percentage Defense'' values and how much damage they actually reduce has been provided below. This is not a comprehensive list and the values may not be fully accurate due to how the game rounds up the damage, making the values occasionally lower.

===Countering Defense===
'''Defense''' can reduce the damage output of most towers significantly.

There are a couple of towers and consumables that can melt the ''Percentage Defense'' value of enemies, allowing your towers to deal more damage. A few certain towers can also ignore defense. There are two types of defense melting towers. The first has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a certain percentage. However, if the [[Pyromancer]], which melts defense by 50%, is decreasing defense of [[Fallen Hero]], which has 50% defense, this does not mean its defense will be lowered to 0%. Instead, it is decreased by 25% defense, as which is 50% of 50% defense. The defense removal can stack, so the [[Pyromancer]] and [[Electroshocker]] can together remove 70% ''Percentage Defense'', but two [[Pyromancer]]s cannot remove 100% ''Percentage Defense''. Instead, only 50% ''Percentage Defense'' can be melted. Additionally, defense melting from burn cannot stack with other burn towers, freeze defense melting cannot stack with other freeze towers and poison defense melting cannot stack with other poison towers.

The second type has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a flat amount. For example, the [[DJ Booth]] at maximum power can melt 25% defense. This means that when melting defense of the [[Fallen Giant]], it will will melt its defense from 60% to 35%.

Both forms of defense melting do not interfere with each other and can stack. For example, if the [[DJ Booth]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 75%, the [[Pyromancer]] will reduce it from 75% to 25%, which is the same decrease (50% less defense) as if [[DJ Booth]] did not affect it. Likewise, if the [[Pyromancer]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 50%, the [[DJ Booth]] will still be able to decrease it by 25%, from 50% to 25%.

The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.
